title: Nosebleed
summary: Sit forward and pinch the soft part of the nose continuously.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Epistaxis
actions: Sit the person upright and leaning slightly forward. Ask them to breathe through the mouth.
Pinch the soft part of the nose just below the bony bridge continuously for 10 to 15 minutes without releasing to check.
Spit out blood that enters the mouth. A cool pack over the nose or cheeks may be used for comfort.
Repeat one period of firm pressure if needed. Seek urgent care if bleeding remains heavy or persistent, follows major trauma, or the person takes anticoagulants.
prohibitions: Do not tilt the head back or lie flat.
Do not pack the nose with tissue or cotton.
Do not release pressure every few minutes to check.
Avoid nose blowing or strenuous activity immediately afterward.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for severe blood loss, breathing difficulty, fainting, or major facial trauma; seek care if bleeding does not stop.
